title: Cooperative pay in Lloyd Hunter's band
summary: Hunter's band split receipts after expenses, so $15 a night was good, bookers took theirs first, and some nights paid two dollars.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Yeah. You know, I never asked you what kind of money you were making.
I know the money wasn't tremendous in those days.
No, it wasn't, it really wasn't. Now, with Lloyd Hunter's band, this is what you would call a consolidated band.
Whatever you make, we split up down --
And what we made, we split it right down the middle.
Because we had to pay for travelling, buying gas and all like that.
For the car, have to take out expense money and split it down the middle.
And if we got $15 a night, that was good.
Yeah, yeah. That's -- especially if you were working five days a week.
They had to get their money. They got theirs in front.
So some nights we might not make but two dollars.
Yeah. Some nights when you'd have a storm or something, you didn't have a -- you got a little percentage of the gate, probably.
And if the gate wasn't good --
If it wasn't good, well, we didn't get anything.
That's right, yeah. So that was always a little chancy, wasn't it?
We'd have to get a guarantee.
